from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Nature of Binary", 
                          ["Binary uses only digits zero and one.", 
                           "Each position represents a power of two.", 
                           "Counting in binary follows a simple pattern."])
        
        # Create initial binary number
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(digit, font_size=72) for digit in ["0", "0", "0"]])
        bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(bits))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Helper to highlight specific bit
        def highlight_bit(idx, color):
            return bits[idx].animate.set_color(color)
            
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # 000 -> 001
        bits1 = VGroup(*[Text(digit, font_size=72) for digit in ["0", "0", "1"]])
        bits1.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).move_to(bits.get_center())
        bits1[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Transform(bits, bits1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 001 -> 010
        bits2 = VGroup(*[Text(digit, font_size=72) for digit in ["0", "1", "0"]])
        bits2.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).move_to(bits.get_center())
        bits2[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Transform(bits, bits2))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 010 -> 011
        bits3 = VGroup(*[Text(digit, font_size=72) for digit in ["0", "1", "1"]])
        bits3.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).move_to(bits.get_center())
        bits3[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        bits3[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Transform(bits, bits3))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # 011 -> 100
        bits4 = VGroup(*[Text(digit, font_size=72) for digit in ["1", "0", "0"]])
        bits4.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).move_to(bits.get_center())
        bits4[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Transform(bits, bits4))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Towers of Hanoi to Binary", [
            "Towers of Hanoi puzzles have specific moves.",
            "Binary counting maps directly to these moves.",
            "Three disks take seven total moves."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display three pegs labeled Peg A, B, C
        peg_a = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*1.0, color=WHITE).add_tip()
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20).next_to(peg_a, DOWN)
        peg_b = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*1.0, color=WHITE).add_tip()
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(peg_b, DOWN)
        peg_c = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*1.0, color=WHITE).add_tip()
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20).next_to(peg_c, DOWN)
        
        pegs = VGroup(VGroup(peg_a, label_a), VGroup(peg_b, label_b), VGroup(peg_c, label_c)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(pegs, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(pegs))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Add 3 disks on Peg A (#1E90FF)
        disk1 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=0.8, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=1)
        disk2 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=1.0, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=1)
        disk3 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=1.2, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=1)
        disks = VGroup(disk3, disk2, disk1).arrange(UP, buff=0).move_to(peg_a.get_bottom() + UP*0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(disks))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight disk 1 as '1', disk 2 as '2', etc.
        t1 = Text("1", font_size=16).move_to(disk1.get_center())
        t2 = Text("2", font_size=16).move_to(disk2.get_center())
        t3 = Text("3", font_size=16).move_to(disk3.get_center())
        labels = VGroup(t3, t2, t1)
        
        self.play(Write(labels))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Disk-Movement Rule", [
            "The disk moving depends on step number.",
            "Look for the rightmost one in binary.",
            "Position of one determines disk size."
        ])
        
        # Draw 3 disks
        disk_colors = ["#40E0D0", "#FF6347", "#FFD700"]
        disks = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            d = Rectangle(width=1.5 - i * 0.3, height=0.3, color=disk_colors[i], fill_opacity=1)
            disks.add(d)
        
        # Place disks on Peg A (Positions D3, E3, F3)
        self.place_at_grid(disks[0], "F3", 1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(disks[1], "E3", 1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(disks[2], "D3", 1.0)
        self.add(disks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#40E0D0"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        indicator = Arrow(start=UP, end=DOWN, color="#FFFF00").next_to(disks[0], UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(indicator))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Show disk moving from Peg A (D3) to Peg C (say D5) - purely visual demonstration
        self.play(disks[0].animate.move_to(self.grid["F5"]), indicator.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Algorithm", [
            "The algorithm shifts disks systematically.",
            "Binary bits toggle as moves occur.",
            "This process reveals a recursive structure."
        ])
        
        # Create recursion tree structure
        tree = VGroup()
        nodes = []
        for i in range(7):
            node = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#D3D3D3")
            nodes.append(node)
            tree.add(node)
            
        # Manually position nodes for tree-like structure
        nodes[0].move_to(self.grid["A4"])
        nodes[1].move_to(self.grid["C2"])
        nodes[2].move_to(self.grid["C6"])
        nodes[3].move_to(self.grid["E1"])
        nodes[4].move_to(self.grid["E3"])
        nodes[5].move_to(self.grid["E5"])
        nodes[6].move_to(self.grid["E7"] if "E7" in self.grid else self.grid["E6"])

        lines = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[4].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[6].get_center(), color="#D3D3D3"),
        )
        
        full_tree = VGroup(lines, tree)
        self.add(full_tree)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(lines[0].animate.set_color("#FF6347"), lines[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"), lines[3].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(lines[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"), lines[4].animate.set_color("#32CD32"), lines[5].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Towers of Hanoi reflects binary counting.", 
            "Recursive problems often have binary solutions.", 
            "Complexity arises from simple binary rules."
        ])
        
        # Create elements
        hanoi_binary = Text("Hanoi = Binary", font_size=40, color="#FFA500")
        self.place_at_grid(hanoi_binary, 'B3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        summary_points = VGroup(
            Text("n disks", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Text("2^n - 1 steps", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(summary_points, 'D2', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(summary_points, color="#FFA500", buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Binary
sections.content: Briefly introduce the binary system as a base-2 counting method (0 and 1). Explain that each bit represents a power of 2, mirroring the structure of branching decisions.

sections.title: Mapping Towers of Hanoi to Binary
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: moving n disks from Peg A to Peg C using Peg B. Explain that the sequence of moves corresponds directly to the binary counting sequence (001, 010, 011, etc.).
sections.example: For 3 disks, the total moves = 2^3 - 1 = 7. Each move corresponds to an integer from 1 to 7 represented in 3 bits.

sections.title: The Disk-Movement Rule
sections.content: Explain the elegant link: The disk that moves at step 'i' is determined by the position of the rightmost '1' in the binary representation of 'i'.
sections.example: In a 3-disk puzzle, at step 4 (Binary 100), the 3rd disk moves because the rightmost '1' is in the 3rd position.

sections.title: Visualizing the Algorithm
sections.content: Show an animation of a monk (The Algorithm) moving disks based on the binary state. The binary bits 'toggle' as the monk completes each move, showing the cyclical nature of the puzzle.
sections.example: A 3-disk stack shifting: Step 1 (001) -> Move smallest disk. Step 2 (010) -> Move second smallest. Step 3 (011) -> Move smallest disk again.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Reinforce that the Towers of Hanoi is not just a game, but a physical manifestation of a binary counter. This highlights how complex recursive problems can be solved through simple binary logic.
sections.example: Summary table: Disks (n) vs Binary sequence length (2^n - 1), demonstrating exponential growth in steps required.
